clue.text: One no longer having a female partner

definitions.text: One no longer having a female partner

parts.words: One no longer having a female partner
parts.note: a straight description of a man whose wife has died, phrased so it might also suggest a dancer or business partner gone

explanation.definitionFit: A man whose wife has died and who has not remarried is a bereaved husband.

clue.text: Part of camera found in town in France

explanation.surface: Somewhere in a French town a camera component turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: The glass element focusing light in a camera shares its name with a mining town in northern France.

clue.text: Drink one quarter lying on one's back

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
I is the Roman numeral for one
NE, north-east, is one of the compass quarters

explanation.surface: Someone sips a quarter-measure of drink while reclining.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine is the formal word for lying face upward.

clue.text: No danger reproducing hormone

indicators.note: reproducing suggests the letters are produced again in a new form, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hormone involved in reproduction is declared safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproducing' rearranges the letters of NO DANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Androgens such as testosterone are male sex hormones.

clue.text: Success football team had on the south coast

parts.note: a win is a success
Chelsea is a London football club

explanation.surface: A football club enjoyed a winning season down by the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' is only a link. Winchelsea is a small town in East Sussex near England's south coast; Chelsea is a Premier League club in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition locates the place rather than naming a synonym: it is an old Cinque Ports town by the English Channel.

clue.text: A French dance? American surely — get it straight!

parts.note: un is the French for a
the twist was a dance craze from 1960s America, as the question invites us to confirm

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether a dance is French or American, followed by an exhortation to sort the matter out.
explanation.walkthrough: The twist, an American dance of the early 1960s, follows UN; the question mark merely confirms its origin.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo the twists in something is to make it straight again.

clue.text: The man I had included is not in the refuge

indicators.note: included means the contraction for I had sits within the pronoun for the man

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
I'd is the contraction of I had
out is the opposite of in, as of someone not at home

explanation.surface: A man has been invited along, but he isn't at the shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideout is a hiding place used as a refuge from pursuers.

clue.text: I can remove twisted net revealing antique

indicators.note: re-move, read as moving again, tells us the letters of I can are shifted around
twisted net is the word net bent out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone untangles a knotted net and finds an old relic beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remove' is read as re-move: I CAN becomes ANCI; 'twisted' turns NET into ENT. 'revealing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient and antique both describe things from long ago.

clue.text: Take what is suitable

explanation.surface: Advice to take only what is fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means seize for oneself; as an adjective it means fitting or proper.

clue.text: Person in church back row is one who delivers goods overseas

indicators.note: back tells us the word row is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a shipper sends freight by sea

explanation.surface: Someone sitting in the back pew of a church turns out to be in the export trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ROW into WOR, which comes before SHIPPER; the surface pretends 'back row' is a church pew.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attending a church service is there to offer worship.

clue.text: Brotherhood?

parts.note: read not as fraternity but as the hood a brother, that is a monk, wears

explanation.definitionFit: A monk's hooded garment is the hood worn by a friar or brother.

clue.text: What a pity it is twice as costly

indicators.note: twice means the word for costly appears two times in a row

parts.note: dear means expensive

explanation.surface: A lament that something now costs double.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled exclamation is a mild expression of regret or dismay.

clue.text: Getting back from the sea

parts.note: reads like retrieving something lost overboard, but means turning tidal land into dry ground

explanation.definitionFit: Draining coastal land to make it usable is called recovering land, as with Dutch polders.

clue.text: Fat film

explanation.surface: A terse comment on a greasy film.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal fat is a lubricating substance, and the 1978 musical with Travolta has this title.

clue.text: Musician who cannot perform on his own

definitions.text: Musician who cannot perform on his own

parts.words: Musician who cannot perform on his own
parts.note: sounds like a nervous player, but describes a pianist whose role is to support a soloist

explanation.definitionFit: This player supports a singer or soloist, so the role exists only alongside another performer.

clue.text: Knowing too much about said questions

parts.note: over can mean about, as in a dispute over money

indicators.note: said tells us the word for questions is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: whys are questions, as in the whys and wherefores

explanation.surface: Someone who knows too much talks about the questions raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' makes WHYS, a plural of questions, sound like WISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Overwise means conceitedly or excessively clever.

clue.text: Vehemence over fur distribution

indicators.note: distribution suggests the letters of over fur are dealt out afresh in another order

explanation.surface: Passions run high over how furs should be handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution' rearranges the letters of OVER FUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean intense passion or zeal.

clue.text: Significance in a sense

explanation.surface: Something important in one sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The import of something and the sense of a word are both what is intended or conveyed.

clue.text: Scold worker about to desert

indicators.note: about means the insect word goes around the word for deserting

parts.note: a worker is a bee, the sterile female of the hive
to rat is to desert one's side

explanation.surface: Someone tells off an employee who is about to walk out.
explanation.definitionFit: To berate someone is to rebuke them angrily.

clue.text: Destined to have poor health?

parts.note: read literally as fated to be sick, it is a phrase for doomed to misfortune

explanation.definitionFit: Doomed or unlucky people are said to have a bad destiny.

clue.text: Fool about with a hard sponge

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of fool are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone messes around with a tough bath sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges FOOL into LOOF; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried fibrous gourd is used as a bath scrubber.

clue.text: Move inside with hesitation for an egg

indicators.note: inside picks the interior letters of the word move, dropping its ends

parts.note: um is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone shifts indoors, hesitating over an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovum is a female reproductive cell.

clue.text: Always pointless

explanation.surface: A two-word comment that something is forever futile.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means forever, and read literally describes something with no tip, so no point.

clue.text: It is served inside

parts.note: reads like a dish served indoors but refers to a sentence done by a prisoner

explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners serve a term of imprisonment behind bars.

clue.text: Provide swimmer with vessel containing tea inside

indicators.note: inside means the vessel word goes within the swimmer word

parts.note: a fish is a swimmer
an urn is a large vessel for tea

explanation.surface: Someone supplies a goldfish with a tea urn.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish someone is to supply or equip them.

clue.text: I'm going back in jeans snagged on a fragrant shrub

indicators.note: in means the reversed pair goes within the rearranged jeans
snagged jeans are torn and pulled out of shape, so their letters are rearranged
going back means I'm is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Someone heading home catches their jeans on a scented bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snagged' turns JEANS into JASNE; 'going back' makes MI from I'M, put 'in' between JAS and NE. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasmine is a climbing shrub with sweet-smelling flowers.
